text:
maria: quick follow-up from the offload RFC review — i'm still fuzzy on the intended shape of the public api for soft-reserves vs host-staging pools. do we expect callers (tenants) to be able to request a 'soft reserve' that pins a percentage of host staging, or should policy be entirely controller-side?
kevin: my take: controller-only. exposing percent-to-pin per-tenant smells like noisy neighbor. keep it declarative (SLAs) not imperative.
sanjay: agree with kevin mostly, but we need a hook for specialized workloads (low-latency embeddings) to opt into reserved lanes. maybe a capability flag rather than a numeric knob.
liz: +1 for capability flag. also mention fragmentation: if we always allocate from global host staging, we end up with interleaved small slabs that kill compaction. i think per-tenant arenas would make compaction + migration simpler.
maria: per-tenant arenas sounds heavy operationally. we'd need limits, eviction tiers, cross-tenant migration policy. can we prototype per-tenant logical arenas that are backed by a shared physical pool? 
dan: that's the thin veneer approach i was suggesting earlier — logical arenas + allocation tags. allocator allocates physical slabs from a shared pool, tags them with owner id. compaction can operate at tag granularity when safe. cheaper than fully isolated arenas.
kevin: question: how do we avoid warmup penalty for tenants with lots of tiny allocations if slabs are tagged? tags don't buy locality unless we consolidate. we need a background consolidator that can migrate hot small allocations into dense tenant-owned slabs. migration = memcpy + remap steps.
sanjay: propose: two-phase mover: 1) pre-copy live objects into new slab, 2) atomically switch metadata pointers, 3) free old slab asynchronously. need to expose a brief lock/window for remap. this is basically compaction-on-write.
maria: can we make that safe across GPU kernels and kv-cache entries? e.g., if a running inference references a pointer while we remap, we must either block or make remap wait for grace period.
liz: we can piggyback on existing request quiesce flow: mark slab draining, disallow new KV-cache entries from being pinned to that slab, wait for in-flight usage count to drop to zero (or timeout) then migrate. that gives bounded disruption.
dan: timeout + exponential backoff for tenants that never drain (bad clients) — fallback is to leave some fragmentation. tradeoff: background compaction cost vs residual fragmentation.
kevin: operational concern: telemetry. we need a compactness metric per-tenant and a TTL-ed historical histogram so SRE can triage noisy tenants. add compactness to tenant dashboard.
maria: agreed. also need an API for tenants to opt into aggressive compaction if they accept CPU/GPU migration overhead (for example nightly). could be boolean name: "allow_background_migration".
sanjay: edge case: pinned device memory (CUDA pinned) vs page-backed host staging migration. migrating pinned GPU buffers is costly — we should prefer moving host-backed pages first and only when that fails consider device-level H2H remap or model fallback.
liz: implementation sketch: allocator exposes APIs:
```
allocate(tenant_id, size, flags) -> token
free(token)
mark_draining(tenant_id, slab_id) -> bool
start_migration(slab_id) -> migrate_id
query_compactness(tenant_id) -> float
```
We keep flags thin: {urgent, capability_embedded_lowlatency, allow_background_migration}.
maria: this is great. can someone jot downsides? performance penalty, complexity in metadata, increased GC cycles. also need to ensure isolation for private deployments (on-prem) where tenants==customers.
dan: downside: cross-node migration for Dedicated clusters — moving slab contents across hosts is expensive; consider a soft-fallback that prefers local compaction and only reassigns ownership if node-level pressure persists.
kevin: +1. also, compatibility path: provide a controller policy that maps tenant SLA -> allocation strategy (shared, soft-reserve, full-isolate). Keep defaults conservative.
sanjay: i'm worried about correctness with asynchronous remap during streaming responses. we should instrument a canary that runs compaction on a small internal tenant first.
maria: ok action items: 1) draft API doc for allocate/free/mark_draining/migrate + semantics (liz), 2) prototype logical arena + tag-based compactor on dev cluster (sanjay + dan), 3) telemetry additions for compactness + migration ops (kevin), 4) controller policy mapping and default values (maria).
liz: i'll start the api doc and include example sequences and edge cases. will post a PR by EOD Friday. :rocket:
offload-bot: migration-job-queue: queued 1 job(s) for compactor-canary (dev-tenant). ETA approx 5m.
kevin: nice — let's keep the canary tiny. set allow_background_migration=true only for the canary. report back perf counters + pre/post latency.
sanjay: i'll pair with dan on the prototype. we'll test cold-warm cycles, embedding latencies, and kv-cache miss rates. expected notes: small regressions under active compaction, big wins after consolidation.
maria: thanks all. we'll sync next week after PR + canary.
